messages:
sam: heads-up — after the fa3 rollout on canary we saw a 12-18% p50 latency increase for short seqs (<=64). digging in now.

lina: thanks for flagging. is this only on au-gpu pool or across all queues?

sam: mostly in the hetero pool (A100 mixed with L4s). dedicated A100-only nodes look fine.

mike: could be workspace allocation falling back to larger fragments? saw more 'alloc failure, retry bigger' lines in logs earlier.

sam: exact log tail i grabbed: ```
E 2026-02-18T13:02:11.123 runtime alloc.c:142 workspace_alloc: no fit for 8192, trying next pool
W 2026-02-18T13:02:11.124 runtime kernel.c:87 kernel_fallback: selected fa2-bf16 slowpath
```

jo: do we have telemetry that maps per-request kernel selection + chosen kernel latency?

natalie: yes we added lightweight kernel tags in trace spans last quarter. i can pull the traces for that time window.

lina: initial theory: v3's workspace sizing changed (alignment/fragmentation) and our kernel selector prefers v3 even when it causes extra allocations on smaller GPUs. selector thresholds were tuned for throughput, not short-latency.

mike: also note v3 has different padding heuristics: it pads to 128 in some cases where v2 padded to 64. that bumps memory churn.

sam: quick experiment idea: add an override that forces kernel_selector to prefer fa2 for seq<=64 on hetero pool, keep v3 default elsewhere. low-risk canary.

jo: agree. can we make it config flag gated per-pool? then we can flip per-queue.

deploy-bot: deploy request accepted by infra pipeline — patch: runtime/kernel_selector: add per_pool kernel_priority override. ci checks passed.

lina: before we flip, would like to run microbench with realistic coalesced batches. last time synthetic tests missed the batch tail behavior. we should replay production sampling for short-seq traffic.

natalie: i'll export a 30m sample from 2026-02-18 12:30-13:00 (short-seq heavy) and run against a patched runtime in the perf cluster.

mike: also add kernel telemetry counters: chosen_kernel, fallback_reason, requested_workspace, allocated_workspace. even simple counters will help correlate.

sam: can someone draft the minimal selector change? prefer fa2 when: (seq_max<=64 && pool_hetero==true && free_fragment_ratio<0.25) — fallback to normal heuristics otherwise.

jo: that rule seems fine but let's avoid hardcoded numerics. expose as per-pool config with defaults matching that rule.

natalie: running replay now, initial run shows p50 down ~10% when forcing fa2 for short seqs on hetero. p99 similar. throughput impact negligible for these weights.

lina: promising. we should still track longer-term: maybe v3 can be tuned for smaller padding or better workspace packing. open question: do we ship quick selector change then do a v3 tuning RFC?

mike: +1 to shipping selector change as hotfix. start a follow-up RFC for kernel memory model and padding alignment; that will be bigger.

sam: i'll open the PR and add a short changelog. can we canary to 10% of hetero pool for 1h then 50%? ops?

infra-bot: canary plan approved: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 3 hours if no regressions. auto-rollback on error spike >5% or latency increase >10%.

lina: also capture a few corner cases: interleaved seqlen batches and kv-cache heavy requests — those were subtle last time. add them to the replay set.

natalie: noted, adding interleaved and kv-heavy slices. will rerun after PR build.

mike: one more note: document the observed delta matrix across GPUs (A100, H100, L4) and across batch sizes 1..8. we should add to the kernel compatibility doc.

sam: thanks team. action items: sam PR + canary, natalie replays and telemetry, lina start RFC outline for v3 padding/workspace, mike update kernel-doc matrix. i'll post status updates here. :thumbsup:
